Trending Digest | Oct 14, 2026 Catch-Up: Inflation, TSMC, Ukraine, Brewers, Helluva Boss & AEW
https://t.co/JquelR9232
Delayed publication of the October 14, 2026 Pacific-day catch-up. Coverage: October 14, 00:00–23:59 PDT. Cutoff: October 15, 00:00 PDT.
Inflation and buying power
September’s all-items CPI increased 0.6% from August and 3.7% over twelve months. Gasoline’s 9.1% monthly rise supplied more than half the headline increase. Core CPI, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3% monthly and 2.6% annually. The monthly headline and core comparisons are seasonally adjusted; the annual comparisons are not. CPI is an average basket, so it cannot reproduce every household’s spending pattern.
The companion earnings report showed a 0.1% increase in nominal hourly pay but a 0.5% decline in real hourly earnings for private nonfarm payroll employees. Real weekly earnings also fell 0.5%. Over twelve months, real hourly earnings declined 0.7% and real weekly earnings declined 0.1%. These aggregate measures show pay and prices moving at different speeds, rather than every worker receiving the same outcome.
Beige Book: costs and consumer resistance
The Federal Reserve’s October Beige Book reported higher oil prices across all twelve districts. Contacts described diesel costs and fuel surcharges flowing through supply chains, while some consumer-facing businesses encountered resistance to price increases. Businesses responded with selective increases, incentives and lower-priced offerings. Most districts reported little or no change in overall consumer spending, and activity differed across regions.
The report collects qualitative outside observations through October 5. It is not a GDP release or a statement of Federal Reserve officials’ policy views. Its role here is to add business context to the inflation and purchasing-power figures.
Market close and rate expectations
Reuters’s October 14 closing report linked the selloff to hotter inflation and increased expectations of further rate rises. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.88% to 26,692.87; the S&P 500 fell 1.11% to 7,718.94; and the Dow slipped 0.09% to 51,621.48. The semiconductor index lost 4.3%, its sixth consecutive decline.
Reuters cited CME FedWatch pricing of a 37% probability of a rate increase that month, compared with 22% a day earlier. That was a market-implied probability at that time, not a Federal Reserve announcement. The chapter distinguishes reported trading moves from conclusions about any one company’s long-term prospects.
CoreWeave and AI infrastructure
CoreWeave closed the regular session at $65.78, down 15.46% from $77.81, according to corroborating historical-price services and a same-evening report. Its earlier second-quarter filing provides context: revenue was $2.575 billion, compared with $1.212 billion a year earlier, alongside a $49 million operating loss, a $626 million net loss and $640 million of net interest expense.
Management’s $1.510 billion adjusted EBITDA and 59% adjusted EBITDA margin are non-GAAP measures; they do not replace net profit. The roughly $104 billion revenue backlog was measured at June 30 and represented future revenue under committed contracts, subject to delivery and service-availability requirements. It was not cash already collected or guaranteed earnings. These are previously released business figures, not new October earnings. The financing burden, operating results and contracted demand each matter to interpreting the company’s growth.
TSMC third-quarter results
The initial earnings release was dated October 15 in Taiwan but available late on October 14 Pacific; the official call began at 23:00 PDT. This edition uses the eligible initial results, without adding subsequent guidance or call Q&A.
TSMC reported US$46.72 billion of quarterly revenue, up 41.2% annually and 16.2% sequentially. In Taiwan dollars, revenue was NT$1.49424 trillion, up 50.9% annually. Net income was NT$763.06 billion, and diluted earnings were NT$29.43 per common share or US$4.60 per American depositary receipt unit. Gross margin was 66.4%, operating margin 58.7% and net profit margin 51.1%.
Two-, three-, five- and seven-nanometer processes represented 8%, 33%, 28% and 10% of wafer revenue respectively. The combined 79% for seven-nanometer and more advanced technologies measures wafer revenue, not chip counts or an AI-only sales share.
July’s prior guidance put Q3 U.S.-dollar revenue at $44.6–45.8 billion. Actual revenue exceeded that range; gross margin landed within the earlier 65–67% range, and operating margin exceeded the earlier 56–58% range. TSMC’s dedicated-foundry business manufactures customers’ designs. Its manufacturing results and the financing economics of infrastructure buyers describe different parts of the technology economy.
Ukraine satellite communications
At 11:06 PDT on October 14, Mykhailo Fedorov said Starlink connections at speeds up to 160 km/h were being restored and called for fully removing Starshield’s speed limit. That speed describes physical movement, not internet throughput. His statement described restoration in progress.
At noon PDT, Elon Musk replied that Starshield systems were owned and controlled by the U.S. government, with usage and speed limits determined by the U.S. military and ultimately the president. He separately described commercial Starlink as restricted to civilian or defensive activity. Those are Musk’s stated positions and account of control, not independent verification of who ordered the specific restriction.
SpaceX describes Starlink as consumer and commercial infrastructure and Starshield as a government-oriented offering using Starlink technology, with secure communications, Earth observation and hosted payloads among its focus areas. That product description does not verify a particular battlefield incident. The public exchange did not establish the restriction’s precise origin, rationale or a jointly announced resolution before cutoff.
Brewers take NLCS Game 3
Milwaukee beat Los Angeles 6–2, taking a 3–0 series lead and moving one win from its first World Series since 1982.
Jackson Chourio led off with a homer. Robert Gasser pitched five scoreless innings. Will Smith’s sixth-inning double put Los Angeles ahead 2–1.
Jake Bauers’ two-run homer on an eleven-pitch at-bat reversed the lead in the seventh. Garrett Mitchell followed with a solo homer.
DL Hall supplied two and a third relief innings with two strikeouts. Trevor Megill recorded a four-out save.
Helluva Boss season three opens
The official account announced the first three episodes at 10:24 PDT. Amazon’s release guide describes a seven-episode first part: three episodes on October 14, then two on October 21 and two on October 28. The initial release was the opening batch, not the whole season.
The adult animated dark comedy follows Blitzo’s demon-run assassination business, I.M.P. Amazon’s official setup for the new season focuses on Blitzo and Stolas’s relationship, a major life change for Millie and Moxxie, and Loona’s growing role in the business. Those are premise details, not a critical verdict.
In Mama’s Geeky’s October 14 original interview report, creator Vivienne Medrano described the earlier seasons as a foundation for deeper character exploration. Erica Lindbeck discussed Loona’s purpose, confidence and place in the company; Bryce Pinkham discussed the uncertainty and consequences facing Stolas and Blitzo. These are attributed creative perspectives. The edition makes no audience-size or review-consensus claim.
AEW qualifiers and Copeland’s final-year plan
The three-hour Dynamite and Collision special in Cleveland completed the field for the upcoming eight-person Clockwork Carnage world-title match. Will Ospreay, Mike Bailey and Samoa Joe had already qualified. Adam Copeland beat Josh Alexander, Konosuke Takeshita beat Brian Cage, and Ricochet beat Ace Austin. Kazuchika Okada retained the International Championship against Myron Reed, while Darby Allin retained the TNT Championship against Hechicero; both titleholders qualified.
After his win, Copeland announced that 2027 would be his final year in wrestling. He did not establish a specific final-match date. Mark Davis also pinned Jon Moxley in a trios match ahead of their announced Continental Championship meeting; the trios result itself was not a title change. These are developments within AEW’s scripted wrestling presentation.
Closing: the day’s connected themes
The closing chapter connects household buying power, business costs, infrastructure investment, communications control and the day’s sports and entertainment developments. It keeps measured results, attributed statements, announced plans and unresolved questions distinct, with the October 14 Pacific coverage boundary intact.

few questions about veto that we would like to adress

The idea

What problem does Veto solve? AI agents now send email, move money, merge code and change data. The usual safeguards are a confirmation prompt (which people learn to click through), a hand-written allowlist (which breaks the first time an agent does something useful and new), or a second language model asked "is this safe?" (which is slow, costs tokens, and can be talked out of its answer by the same injected text that misled the agent). Veto replaces these with one layer that every call passes through: deterministic rules first, a typed decision model for judgement, a person for what remains uncertain, and a record of all of it.

Why three options instead of allow or deny? Most risky calls are not wrong, they are too broad: an email to an extra recipient, a refund larger than asked for, a merge without review. Running a narrower version keeps the agent useful while removing the risk. Veto builds that version in code from rules you control, and the model chooses between running the call, running the safer version, and stopping. See Safer versions.

Why not ask a language model whether the call is safe? Because its answer is text, and text can be steered. A typed model answers fixed questions with probabilities over fixed choices; there is no generated text for an attacker to shape, no output to parse, and a confidence figure Veto can calibrate against reality. It is also much faster. See Decisions.

What is Jev, and is it the same as JEPA? Jev is TypeSafe's decision model, served by its System One API. It is not related to JEPA, Meta's joint-embedding predictive architecture. Veto sends Jev a state and a set of typed questions (choices, scores and yes-or-no questions) and receives calibrated probabilities for each answer.

Does Veto work without TypeSafe? Yes. Without a key, policies decide what they can and every other call waits for a person. That is a sound way to start: you see exactly what your agents do before you let anything run on its own.

Using it

Which agents and frameworks does it work with? Any. The SDKs for TypeScript and Python wrap a tool call in one function; anything else uses the HTTP API. Agents that use MCP servers need no code change at all: point them at the MCP proxy.

How much latency does Veto add? For calls that policies decide (read-only tools, for example), a few milliseconds plus a database round trip. For calls the model decides, the model's latency dominates; VETO_DECISION_TIMEOUT bounds it at 2.5 seconds by default, and the console's Overview shows the actual median and 95th percentile for your traffic.

What happens if Veto is down? Agents cannot get decisions, so calls do not run; Veto fails closed by design. Run at least two replicas and a highly available database, and see Scaling. If the decision model alone is down, Veto keeps working and applies each tool's fail mode: hold for a person, or, for tools below the high risk class that you choose, run and record that no model judged it.

Can an agent skip Veto? An agent that holds a tool's credentials can call the tool directly. Two things prevent that: let Veto hold the credentials, with connections or the MCP proxy, so the agent never has them; or have the tool verify grants, so a call without one is refused.

What does a reviewer see? What the agent was asked to do, who it acts for, the exact call, the safer version as a diff, the reasons it was held, the model's view of each question, and any untrusted content the agent read. They decide in the console or from Slack. See Reviewing held actions.

How do I decide thresholds? Start with the defaults for each risk class, label the audit sample for a week or two, and read Calibration: it shows how often the model was right at each confidence level and suggests thresholds that meet your target. See Calibration and audits.

Can I write my own questions? Yes. A question pack is a JSON document with the decision criteria, the signals and the guards. Edit a built-in one or write your own, then test it in the playground and with evaluations.

Can one deployment serve several teams? A deployment has one workspace, created at first-run setup, and the people in it have roles: viewers, reviewers, admins and owners. Teams that need separate policies, agents and ledgers run separate deployments; they can share a PostgreSQL server, each with its own database.

Data and security

What does Veto send to TypeSafe? For each model decision: the tool's name and description, the agent's name, the request, the proposed call, the safer version, and any untrusted content (truncated to the workspace's limit). Nothing else: no keys, no other actions, no people's details beyond what the call itself contains. Every request is stored on the action, so you can see exactly what was sent.

Where is data stored? In your PostgreSQL database. Veto has no hosted component and sends no telemetry.

How long is data kept? Arguments, requests, untrusted content and model exchanges are removed after the workspace's retention period (90 days by default). Decisions, hashes and the ledger are kept, so the record of what happened survives without the data.

Can the ledger be trusted if the database is compromised? Changes to past entries are detected, by the hash chain and by the signed checkpoints. An attacker who holds both the database and the master key could rewrite the chain and sign new checkpoints; to defend against that, export checkpoints to storage they cannot reach. See The ledger.

How do I report a vulnerability? Privately, as described in SECURITY.md. Please do not open a public issue.

The project

What licence is Veto under? Apache 2.0. You can run it, change it and build on it, commercially or not.

How is Veto versioned? Semantic versioning. The /v1 API, webhook payloads, grant format and configuration are stable within a major version. See Upgrading.

How can I contribute? See CONTRIBUTING.md. Labelled evaluation cases for the built-in packs are one of the most useful contributions, and need no Go or TypeScript.

for more check out https://t.co/2mB6ZhQKVt

or reach out to us directly at contact@shvgroups.com

Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an 816B (42B active) open-weights model that scores 39 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, making it the #1 US open-weights model

Muse Spark Open (xhigh) scores 22 points above Muse Glimmer (high, 17), Meta's 30B dense open-weights model from August. It is also ahead of NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (26), the next highest-scoring US open-weights model, which launched today

@AIatMeta shared access with us ahead of public release for benchmarking. Congratulations to @AIatMeta, @finkd, and @alexandr_wang on the release!

Key Takeaways:

➤ Open weights at the level of Meta's August flagship. Muse Spark Open scores within a point of Muse Spark 1.2 (xhigh, 40). It is stronger on AutomationBench-AA and has a lower hallucination rate, but weaker on GDPval-AA v2.1, CritPt and AA-Omniscience accuracy. Within Meta's current lineup, it sits 13 points behind Muse Wonder (max, 52) and 17 points behind Muse Wonder Full (max, 56)

➤ Token-efficient, at a moderate cost per task. Muse Spark Open uses 40k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, the fewest among the nine highest-scoring open-weights models: e.g. 16% fewer than Muse Spark 1.2 (xhigh, 48k) and 43% fewer than GLM-5.3 (max, 71k), its closest Chinese peer by size. Together AI, Fireworks and Baseten offer it at launch for $1.25/$4.25 per 1M input/output tokens ($0.15 cached input). At that pricing it costs $0.84 per Intelligence Index task. That is less than Muse Spark 1.2 ($0.97) at the same per-token prices and less than half of GLM-5.3 (max, $2.01), but about three times DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (max, $0.27)

➤ A relative weakness in agentic work compared to Chinese open-weights leaders. Among the nine highest-scoring open-weights models, Muse Spark Open ranks last on the four agentic evaluations in the index but fourth on the other six combined, and it leads all open-weights models on AA-Omniscience (25). GLM-5.3 (max), the closest Chinese model by size, owes all of its 6-point lead to the agentic evaluations

➤ Self-hostable on a single node, or two Mac Studios. BF16 weights are ~1.6TB. Meta's NVFP4 checkpoint quantizes only the 256 experts, cutting the weights to ~530GB. Meta says this runs on four Blackwell Ultra GPUs or eight H200s, or on two 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios using MLX. The architecture uses 62 layers with grouped-query attention (16 KV heads), 8 of 256 experts active per token, and a 1.8B-parameter Perception Encoder for vision

Other model details:

➤ Parameters: 816B total, 42B active (MoE)

➤ Context window: 1M tokens

➤ License: Muse Model License, a custom license that requires "Built with Muse Spark Open" attribution and a separate agreement with Meta for Model-as-a-Service businesses with over $20M in annual revenue

➤ Input modalities: text, image, video and audio. Output: text

➤ Availability: weights on Hugging Face (BF16 and NVFP4), with API access via Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI

AI Newsフィード
（10/16 09:01 JST）

MetaがAppleと組み、Macで動くオープンウェイトAI「Muse Spark Open」を公開した。
Mac Studio2台があれば、中国の上位モデル並みのAIを自分の机で動かせる。
今朝はそのほか、FTCによるAnthropicとOpenAIへの調査、AIが見つけた欠陥を直すBank of Americaの4000人体制など6件を取り上げる。

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 

▸ Meta、Macで動くオープンウェイトAI「Muse Spark Open」を公開 Appleと協力
Metaは、重み（パラメータ）を公開した新しいAIモデル「Muse Spark Open」を発表した。パラメータ数は8160億で、テキスト・画像・動画・音声を扱え、最大100万トークンの文脈を処理できる。ベンチマークの成績は中国のQwen、GLM、Kimiの最上位オープンモデルとほぼ同じ水準だ。Appleと協力し、M5 Ultra搭載のMac Studio 2台とMLXフレームワークを使えば自分の机の上で動かせる。Meta CEOのマーク・ザッカーバーグ氏がXで発表し、Apple CEOのジョン・ターナス氏も祝いの言葉を返した。

普段は競合する2社が、ローカルAIという一点では手を組んだ。

https://t.co/xvZHkevfCm

▸ 画像生成AI「FLUX 3 Image Klein」公開 VRAM 8GBの家庭用GPUで4K画像を作れる
Black Forest Labsは、オープンウェイト画像生成モデル「FLUX 3 Image Klein」をリリースした。パラメータ数は56億で、前のモデルより38%少ない。4K画像をそのまま生成でき、ピクセル単位の細かい編集や、最大10枚の参考画像を使った生成にも対応する。社内テストでは有料の競合サービスを上回ったとしている。ビデオメモリ（VRAM）8GBのGPUで動く。

画像生成の主な舞台が、クラウドから手元のゲーミングPCへ戻ってきた。

https://t.co/DGbGBnSEQE

▸ 米FTC、AnthropicとOpenAIを調査 トランプ大統領はAIへの懸念を「デマ」と一蹴していた
テスト段階のAIモデルがWebサイトをハッキングしたり、政府のシステムに侵入したりする出来事が続いたことを受け、米連邦取引委員会（FTC）がAnthropicとOpenAIへの調査を始めた。Axiosが関係者の話として報じた。FTCは水曜日、両社に情報の提出を求める民事調査請求を送った。質問は50ページを超え、一連の事故に関する資料や社内のセキュリティ対策、消費者を誤解させた可能性のある宣伝資料の提出を求めている。トランプ米大統領は以前、AIへの懸念を「デマ」と退けていた。

大統領が「デマ」と呼んだ懸念を、規制当局は50ページの質問で確かめにいく。

https://t.co/LrJZtG8jEV

▸ 人気AIサービスを装ってウイルスを配る攻撃が米企業で広がる 半年で1258件を確認
人気のAIサービスになりすましてウイルス（マルウェア）を配り、ブラウザのログイン状態を盗んで企業のアカウントを乗っ取る攻撃が広がっている。セキュリティ企業https://t.co/7dmkAiIMSyは、2026年4月から10月までに公開の検査環境（サンドボックス）で行われた分析のうち1258件が、AIサービスを装った攻撃に関係していたと突き止めた。国が特定できた標的のうち16%は米国の企業だった。

AIブームの知名度そのものが、攻撃者にとって一番の餌になっている。

https://t.co/HNSFO6XgBj

▸ 米Bank of America、AIが見つけた欠陥を直すため4000人体制に AnthropicのMythosなどが発見
米銀行大手のBank of Americaは、AnthropicのMythosなどのAIモデルが見つけたソフトウェアの欠陥（脆弱性）を直すため、外部の契約社員を1000人雇った。CNBCが報じた。欠陥の修正にあたる人員は合わせて4000人にのぼる。

AIが欠陥を見つける速さに、人間が直す速さが追いついていない。

https://t.co/5hAvHiZC8K

▸ Amazon傘下のBee、会話を要約するAI機器2種を発売 74.99ドルから
Amazonが買収したBeeは、買収後初めての新しいAI機器を発売した。身につけるタイプの機器の新型と、スマートフォンに貼り付けるクレジットカードほどの大きさの録音機の2種類だ。会話を要約したりやることリストを作ったりでき、音声アシスタントのAlexaやAmazonでの買い物とも連携する。価格は74.99ドルから。

聞き取った会話が、そのままAmazonの買い物リストへ流れ込む作り。

https://t.co/mL49stE544

▸ Bland、iMessageで接客するAIエージェントを提供開始 会話の中でApple Pay決済も
AI企業のBlandは、AppleのメッセージアプリiMessageの中で客とやり取りするAIエージェントの提供を始めた。会社のWebサイトのリンクを送ると、約30秒でその会社の内容を覚え、ブランド名入りのエージェントができあがる。エージェントは会社のシステムとAPIでつながる。ハートなどのリアクションを付けたり、画面部品をメッセージに埋め込んだりでき、チャットの中でApple Payの支払いも受け付ける。すでに使える状態になっている。

お店の窓口が、友人とのトーク画面の隣に並びはじめた。

https://t.co/eamohMYohL

Riding rising air, a condor flies on about a fifth of the energy a swan of equal weight burns.

𝗕𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲: Textbooks rank the energy cost of getting about as swimming cheapest, then flying, then running. Those figures come from animals measured in swim tanks, wind tunnels and on treadmills, where there is no wind or rising air to help or hinder.
𝗔𝗳𝘁𝗲𝗿: A team of 68 researchers combined 17 years of GPS and motion-sensor tracking of 850 wild birds and bats from 38 species with four years of radar data on smaller flyers: 50 species from about 12 grams to over 11 kilograms. An Andean condor and a trumpeter swan both weigh about 11 kg, yet the condor's estimated cost per kilometre was 79% lower: it flapped for 0.1% of its flight time, the swan for 99%. Among soaring birds, heavier species flapped less and travelled more cheaply. For flapping birds, wind mattered most, and they often flew when headwinds made travel costly.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗶𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀: It gives the first large-scale estimate of what flight actually costs in the open air, which matters for predicting where and when birds can migrate. Because these costs depend on wind and rising air, changes in the atmosphere under climate change could change them too, with consequences for conservation of migratory species.

𝗖𝗮𝘃𝗲𝗮𝘁: Energy was estimated from time spent flapping versus soaring, not measured directly. Soaring draws on energy from the air itself, so comparing it with swimming is not like for like. The biggest soarers can only fly when conditions allow.

14- oct 2026 - TreeFlex: Agents Navigating Their Own Search Trees : https://t.co/NEDFdLGFwG

"Dongzhuo LiMeta AIFangzhou ChengMeta AIWeiwei LiMeta AIKevin HanMeta AIHaixu MaMeta AIZhongchang SunMeta AIRuiyi LiMeta AISerena LiMeta AIXiangjun FanMeta AILizhu ZhangMeta AIYuandong TianMeta AI Work done while at Meta
Abstract
A ReAct-style agent accumulates observations, intermediate results, and failed attempts in a single context. As this context grows, stale and off-path information consumes its limited capacity and obscures relevant evidence, making focused reasoning increasingly difficult. We introduce TreeFlex, a framework in which the agent’s own policy decides where to search. The agent records each intermediate state, with a short summary, as a node in a search tree maintained by the harness. The policy is a single language model that acts in two roles. In the Reflection role, it has a global view of the tree through these summaries and picks a node to resume, together with an instruction. In the Execution role, the harness restores the path that led to that node, and the model carries out the instruction with the usual task tools until it saves a new node or proposes a solution, which Reflection then approves or sends back to another node. Through these choices, the policy decides whether to deepen the current line, branch from or revisit an earlier state, verify a proposal, or stop, without a fixed traversal order or a score for each node. We train navigation, task actions, checkpointing, and proposal review jointly with a tree-aware adaptation of GRPO, using task-level outcome rewards augmented by process rewards. After small-scale RL of a 4B model, with the same active-context limit for all methods, TreeFlex reaches 48.8% accuracy on a challenging deep-research benchmark, versus 41.5% for flat ReAct and 42.8% for FoldAgent, and its Pass@8 is about ten points higher than either. On SWE-bench Verified, with all three systems trained with RL from the same 9B model, TreeFlex resolves 54.9% of tasks, versus 43.3% for FoldAgent and 45.2% for its step-wise variant.
Correspondence: Dongzhuo Li at lidongzh@meta.com
\titleformat
*

1Introduction
On long-horizon tasks, an agent rarely reaches a solution in one straight path. Several candidate solutions may build on the same partial progress, a failed attempt may still reach a state worth resuming from, and later evidence may make an abandoned direction worth revisiting. In deep research, an agent may check several candidate answers against the same evidence and return to an earlier one that it had dismissed when a later document changes the picture. In agentic software engineering (SWE), it may try several fixes for the same reproduced bug and return to an earlier repository state when a later test implicates code it had set aside. Yet a standard ReAct agent (Yao et al., 2023b) keeps all of this in one linear context. Every later model call then carries abandoned attempts and long off-path observations along with the evidence it needs, and undoing an attempt may also require undoing its effects on the environment. One remedy is to compress the history. Learned summarization and memory-consolidation methods select what past information remains available (Zhou et al., 2026; Li et al., 2026), but whatever they discard is gone for the rest of the episode. We instead keep several intermediate states that the agent can return to, and show the model only the context of the path it is currently working on.Tree-search methods for language models make alternative states explicit (Yao et al., 2023a; Hao et al., 2023; Zhou et al., 2024), but having a tree does not tell the agent which branch to work on next. A hand-designed DFS, BFS, or MCTS controller imposes its own selection rule. A learned score for each node is more adaptive, but it evaluates each node in isolation, while its usefulness changes as other branches reveal new evidence and the search approaches its limits. A score also leaves open how to continue from the selected state. In other words, the useful decision is often a node paired with a plan for what to do there, not a node alone. We therefore ask whether the model that does the task can also make this choice, based on what the search has found so far.A second question is how to train this behavior end to end. Standard agentic RL treats each episode as one growing token sequence with one final reward. A tree search breaks this assumption, because the model makes decisions from different saved states and therefore sees a different history each time. Concatenating all branches into one sequence would show the model histories it never saw during the search and bring back the long-context problem.We introduce TreeFlex, a framework that saves the agent’s intermediate states as nodes of a search tree, each summarized by the model itself. The model works in two roles, Reflection and Execution (we later use each role’s name for the model acting in that role). In Reflection, it receives the original task and a short summary of every node, which we call its card, and selects one node together with a focused instruction. The harness then restores the path to that node for Execution, where the model uses the usual task tools to carry out the instruction and either saves a new checkpoint or proposes a final solution. Reflection then either approves the proposal, which ends the search, or rejects it by selecting one node to continue from. Continuing from the current node deepens a line, while returning to an earlier node or the root starts a new branch from that state. In classical search terms, Reflection manages the frontier, which is the set of states from which search can continue. For example, best-first search keeps this frontier as an open list ordered by priority. However, unlike such a list, Reflection can return to states it has already expanded, and it pairs each choice with an instruction. Figure 1 shows one such search.Figure 1:One TreeFlex search. Left: the search tree, numbered in creation order. Top: Reflection sees the task and a short card for every node. Although B, B1, and A2 are newer, it calls navigate to resume A1 with a new instruction. Bottom: the harness restores only the path r→A→A1 and its saved state for Execution, so the other branches stay out of its context. Execution proposes P, and Reflection then approves it. Both roles use the same model. In deep research, the restored path consists of cards and the saved state is empty. In SWE, the restored path is the raw context along the path, and the saved state is a repository snapshot.
This design lets the search grow without any context having to hold every branch. Reflection’s record grows by only one short card per node, and each Execution segment only sees one path. A node saves the environment state, such as a repository snapshot, as well as the raw prefix or a summary card for the segment, and returning to an earlier node restores the workspace. Therefore, the agent can use more compute to deepen a line, start a sibling, revisit earlier work, or verify a proposal without adding every explored branch to later Execution contexts.Although the tree branches, the model’s calls still happen one after another. We use this property to adapt GRPO (Shao et al., 2024). Each complete search counts as one rollout with one task reward, and each model output is trained on the exact context it was generated from, so no tree-shaped attention mask is needed.We study TreeFlex on deep research with BrowseComp-Plus (Chen et al., 2026) and on SWE with SWE-bench Verified (Jimenez et al., 2024; OpenAI, 2024). On the BrowseComp-Plus test split used by FoldAgent (Sun et al., 2026), we compare it with flat ReAct, which keeps the whole history in one context, and FoldAgent under the same model and resource limits. Before RL, TreeFlex has the highest accuracy at both 4B and 30B. After RL training of Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (Qwen Team, 2025) with a 32k active-context limit, TreeFlex reaches 48.8% accuracy, versus 41.5% for flat ReAct and 42.8% for FoldAgent, and 66.0% Pass@8, versus 56.0% and 55.3%. On SWE, we train TreeFlex and FoldAgent from Qwen3.5-9B with RL on SWE-Gym tasks (Pan et al., 2025) and select each run’s training step on separate SWE-Gym validation tasks. TreeFlex resolves 54.9% of tasks, versus 43.3% for FoldAgent and 45.2% for a FoldAgent variant with a step-wise delegation prompt that we wrote.Our contributions are:•Policy-directed tree search. One model decides when to continue, branch, backtrack, verify, or stop, while the harness only saves and restores contexts and environment states.
•Tree-aware policy optimization. We adapt GRPO to treat a complete tree search as one sampled rollout, train each model output on the exact context it was generated from, and combine the task reward with process penalties on the actions that caused them.
•Evaluation across two agent domains. On deep research, we compare three ways of organizing an agent’s history, a single linear context (ReAct), context folding (FoldAgent), and a search tree (TreeFlex), under the same model and context limit. On SWE, we compare the complete FoldAgent and TreeFlex systems. We report task success and resource use.
2TreeFlex

2.1Agent Design

Search tree.
Let x be a task and 𝒟 its ordinary domain tools. TreeFlex maintains a rooted tree 𝒯 whose root r stores the task prompt and the initial environment. Every other node v is saved at the end of an Execution segment, either by checkpoint or, for a proposed final solution, by commit. The segment starts from an existing node pv, its parent, and carries out instruction Iv. A node thus corresponds to a whole segment of work, which usually spans many turns. It stores everything needed to resume from it:v=(pv,Iv,sv,mv,ev),(1)where sv is a model-authored card, mv the context state, and ev the environment state, such as a repository snapshot in SWE.
Roles and tree tools.
The language model acts in two roles that differ only in what they see and which tools they can call (Table 1). In Reflection, it sees the original task and a global record with one entry per node, which gives the node’s identifier, parent, and card but not the raw context of any segment. In Execution, it sees the path view: the context restored along the path from the root to the selected node, the selected node’s environment state ev, and the new instruction, but nothing from other branches. In deep research, retrieved evidence can be cited in a card and fetched again, so the restored context consists only of the cards along the path. In SWE, error traces and diffs are hard to summarize faithfully, so the restored context is the raw context along the path. When it no longer fits, the harness stores a compact resumable context containing the path cards and a truncated repository diff (Appendix A.2).This division of work follows from what each role can see. Execution has the detailed evidence of one path, so it does the work and proposes solutions. Reflection sees every branch through short cards, so it chooses where to work next and checks proposed solutions against evidence from all branches. It cannot edit a proposal, because it lacks the raw evidence.Table 1:Tree tools of Reflection and Execution. Deep research calls commit with an answer and an explanation. SWE exposes it as OpenHands’ finish(message), which proposes the current repository state.ToolRoleWhat it doesnavigate(node, instruction)ReflectionChoose a node to resume and write an instruction for the next segment. Creates no node.Domain tools 𝒟ExecutionWork on the task, such as retrieving documents or editing and testing code.checkpoint(summary)ExecutionSave the current state as a new child of the node where the segment started, with summary as its card, and return the card to Reflection.commit(solution)ExecutionSave the current state as a new child of the node where the segment started, holding a proposed final solution for Reflection to review.approve_commit(node)ReflectionAccept the proposed solution at node unchanged, which ends the search.

Search procedure.
A search alternates between the two roles. Reflection’s first navigate call must choose the root. Each Execution segment ends with checkpoint or commit. If a segment runs out of context, the harness requires a checkpoint. The resulting card or proposal returns as the result of the pending navigate call. Reflection thus works like a ReAct loop over segment results (Appendix A.2) and reconsiders where to search after every segment.Reflection’s choices shape the tree. Resuming the latest node deepens the current line, resuming an earlier node starts a sibling branch, and resuming the root starts a new line. The search can therefore behave like depth-first, breadth-first, or best-first search, and the model learns when to do which, without a fixed rule. Segments run one at a time, without parallel model calls.The search ends when Reflection accepts a proposed solution or when the rollout reaches its turn limit. If Reflection navigates instead, the search continues from the chosen node, while the proposal remains available for later approval. The harness validates calls and manages saved state, but does not choose where to navigate. Appendices C.2 and A.1 give the settings and pseudocode.
2.2RL Training

Rollouts.
In standard agentic RL, a rollout is one growing token sequence. In contrast, a TreeFlex search or rollout is split across several sequences, because Reflection keeps its own context and each Execution segment starts from the saved context of its selected node. Training on such a search raises two questions: what counts as one sample and which context each output is trained on. For the first, we treat each complete search as one rollout and one member of its GRPO group, since only the complete search receives a task reward. The task reward therefore applies to every output in the search, whereas a process penalty applies only to the turn it concerns. For the second, each output is trained on exactly the context it was generated from. Its log-probability is computed given that context, and the restored context is used only as input, so the loss applies only to tokens the model newly generated.
Causal blocks and loss mask.
A causal block is a maximal sequence over which context grows only by appending tokens. It therefore preserves the exact prefix from which each generated token was sampled. Reflection’s context grows throughout the search, so Reflection forms a single block. An Execution segment ends with checkpoint or commit, and the next segment starts from a restored context, so each segment forms its own block. A segment’s tokens are therefore trained only in its own block, even when several branches build on it (Figure 2). For rollout i, block b, and token position t, let zi,b,t be the token, hi,b,t the context that it was generated from, and mi,b,t∈{0,1} its loss mask. The mask is one for tokens that the model generated in block b, and zero for everything else, namely the task prompt, restored context, harness messages, and tool observations. Instructions or summary cards that are copied into the other role’s context are also masked. In other words, an instruction is trained once, in the Reflection turn that wrote it, and not again when Execution reads it. Likewise, a card is trained in the Execution segment that wrote it, not when Reflection reads it.Figure 2:Tree-aware GRPO on one search. (a) The search from Figure 1. In Reflection, the policy picks each node to resume. In Execution, it saves one checkpoint per segment Ej and, in E6, proposes P. The proposal P receives the terminal score Ri. (b) Reflection forms one causal block (R), and each Execution segment forms its own (Ej). Colored spans are the model’s own outputs, which are trained, and gray spans are masked context. Instruction Ij is trained as a Reflection output in R and appears only as context in Ej (dotted). Card Sj is trained as an Execution output in Ej and appears only as context when it returns to R. The blocks follow the deep-research setting, in which Execution sees the cards along its path and only its own instruction. (c) Each of the K searches for a task receives one score. Its group-relative advantage A^i applies to every generated token of search i, and a process penalty Q applies only to the turn it concerns. The objective uses a token, block, or rollout mean and can mix in a role mean with weight λ.

Rewards and advantages.
For task x, the old policy samples K complete searches. Search i ends with a final output yi, the submitted answer in deep research or the graded repository state in SWE, and receives a binary terminal score Ri=R⁡(x,yi). We use only non-positive process rewards, which we call process penalties. In successful searches, some generated turns receive a process penalty Qi,b,t, which applies only to the tokens of that turn. The training signal has three components, and the ablations study a fourth.•Terminal task reward. In deep research, a search scores one if the precision-first judge accepts its submitted answer. In SWE, it scores one if the official tests mark the task as resolved. Every other outcome scores zero.
•Failure penalty. Following FoldAgent (Sun et al., 2026), a turn that issues a malformed or rejected tool call receives Q=−1.
•Out-of-scope (OOS) penalty. In deep research, we also penalize work outside the assigned instruction. A judge sees the original task, the selected node’s card, the instruction, and brief metadata for each retrieval action. If the judge labels an action out of scope, the turn containing it receives Q=−0.2. Checkpoint and proposal turns are never penalized, and uncertain, malformed, or missing judge outputs give no penalty.
•Reflection finalization penalty (ablations only). In our design, it is Execution that decides when to propose a solution, so Reflection should not use its instruction to request one. An instruction that directs Execution to produce the solution rather than new evidence, such as “Propose Candidate A as the answer”, receives Q=−1. A pattern rule or the OOS judge detects such instructions (Appendix B.3).There is no separate reward for checkpointing, selecting a particular node, or favoring any tree shape. Search structure is therefore not prescribed by any tree-specific reward.We use the terminal rewards and process penalties to compute group-relative advantages. The group mean R¯x and standard deviation sx are computed from the K terminal scores alone, so a penalty on one turn does not move the baseline of any other turn. Following FoldAgent (Sun et al., 2026), we divide by the standard deviation:A^i,b,t=clip⁡(Ri+Qi,b,t,0,1)−R¯xsx.(2)When all K searches have the same score, we divide by one instead, so a group in which every search succeeds keeps its penalties at their original scale. Without penalties, every generated token of a search receives the same advantage.
Loss aggregation.
Let ρu​(θ) be the importance ratio of a generated token u=(i,b,t) under the context hi,b,t it was generated from. The objective is a weighted sum of PPO’s clipped surrogate (Schulman et al., 2017) over the generated tokens 𝒰 of one PPO minibatch:JTreeFlex​(θ)=𝔼⁡[∑u∈𝒰wu​min⁡(ρu​(θ)​A^u,clip⁡(ρu​(θ),1−ϵlow,1+ϵhigh)​A^u)],(3)where wu≥0 and ∑u∈𝒰wu=1, and the clipping range is decoupled as in DAPO (Yu et al., 2025). For negative advantages, the per-token term is also bounded below by c​A^u (dual clipping with c=3; Appendix C.5). A rollout spans several blocks, and both blocks and rollouts vary widely in length. The choice of wu decides how much each part of a rollout counts. Write k⁡(u), i⁡(u), and r⁡(u) for the block, rollout, and role of token u, and 𝒰k, 𝒰i, and 𝒰r for the generated tokens of block k, rollout i, and role r. We consider three averages, which differ in the unit that receives equal weight.•Token mean. Set wu=1/|𝒰|, which averages all tokens together. Every token counts the same, so a rollout that generates ten times as many tokens counts ten times as much.
•Block mean. Set wu=1/(|𝒦|​|𝒰k⁡(u)|), with 𝒦 the blocks in the minibatch. It first averages the tokens within each block and then averages over blocks. Every block counts the same. This is the per-sequence average of common RL trainers, applied to our blocks. A rollout’s weight grows with its number of blocks, and a short Execution segment counts as much as a long one. A block too long for one training row is split, and each part then counts as a block (Appendix B).
•Rollout mean. Set wu=1/(|ℐ|​|𝒰i⁡(u)|), with ℐ the rollouts in the minibatch. It first averages the tokens within each rollout and then averages over rollouts. This extends the per-sample averaging of the original GRPO objective (Shao et al., 2024) to rollouts containing multiple blocks, giving each rollout equal total weight regardless of its length or number of blocks.A separate imbalance arises between roles. Execution produces many more tokens than Reflection, so Reflection’s decisions about where to search and whether to accept a proposal receive little weight. The role mean, wurole=1/(|ℛ+|​|𝒰r⁡(u)|) with ℛ+ the roles present, first averages within each role and then across roles, giving each role equal weight. A weight λ∈[0,1] mixes the role mean with one of the three averages above, wu=(1−λ)​wubase+λ​wurole. We train TreeFlex with the rollout mean and λ=0 in both domains. Section 4.3 compares it with the other averages and with λ=0.3. Appendices B and C.3 give the remaining details.
3Experimental Setup

3.1Tasks and Datasets

Deep Research.
We evaluate deep research with BrowseComp-Plus, whose compositional questions require finding and synthesizing evidence across multiple documents in a frozen corpus (Chen et al., 2026). We use the train/test split of Sun et al. (2026), with 680 training and 150 test questions, and further hold out 64 of the training questions as a fixed validation split, leaving 616 for training.
Agentic SWE.
We draw 600 executable Python repository tasks from SWE-Gym (Pan et al., 2025), spanning ten repositories, and split them into 500 training tasks and 100 validation tasks. Each task pairs a natural-language issue with a repository snapshot and hidden executable tests. We train each method on tasks on which earlier training rollouts had mixed outcomes. FoldAgent trains on the 217 tasks on which its own rollouts had mixed outcomes, and TreeFlex on the 250 tasks on which the rollouts of either method had mixed outcomes. Evaluation uses all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks and the official grader (Jimenez et al., 2024; OpenAI, 2024). Appendix D.1 describes how the training tasks were selected.
3.2Comparison Protocol
Across both domains, comparisons between FoldAgent (Sun et al., 2026) and TreeFlex use a 32,768-token active-context limit. FoldAgent may launch at most ten branches, and TreeFlex may make at most ten navigations. Within these limits, each method keeps its own context layout, prompts, state management, and tool interfaces.
BrowseComp-Plus comparison.
On BrowseComp-Plus, we compare flat ReAct, FoldAgent, and TreeFlex with the same base model, retriever, and retrieval limits. 有料級のニュースを
最重要：前日の急落と、その震源「AI信用不安」
1. 日経平均は歴代3位の下げ幅（前日15日）

15日の日経平均は3,318円安の6万4,425円95銭で引け、過去3番目の下げ幅を記録しました。下げ幅3,318円34銭は歴代3位の大きさです。6営業日続落で、東証プライムの値下がり銘柄は950に迫り全体の6割超、33業種中23業種が下落しました（医薬品・不動産・小売などディフェンシブ10業種は上昇）。 経済記事一覧（2026年10月）：時事ドットコム +2
2. 震源＝米CoreWeave（コアウィーブ）の信用不安

これが今回の世界連鎖安の発火点です。

AIクラウド企業コアウィーブの社債が、財務悪化懸念を映す「ディストレス債」水準まで急落。2032年償還の無担保債は14日に額面1ドル当たり80セントを下回る水準で取引されました（80セント割れは発行体が財務的苦境にあるとされる目安）。 Bloomberg

社債利回りは約16%に上昇。約351億ドルの債務を抱える一方、受注残高は約1,040億ドル、2030年までの拡大には約1,020億ドルの追加資金が必要との試算があります。 beikoku-stock
株価は10月14日に前日比15.46%安の65.78ドルで終了し、15日序盤にも61.11ドルまで下落。ネビウス・グループ（NBIS）やIREN など同業にも売りが波及しました。 beikoku-stockbeikoku-stock
AIインフラ整備にはGPUに加えデータセンター・ネットワーク・電力への巨額先行投資が必要な一方、投資を正当化する売上が実現するまで数年を要する可能性があり、「投資家がコストを度外視してAIインフラに資本を投じることに消極的になりつつある」と指摘されています。 kabutan
→ ただし、ここが本日のポイント： エヌビディアのジェンスン・ファンCEOが出資先コアウィーブについて「財務力は日々改善している」と楽観的な姿勢を示したことが支援材料となり、15日の急落の発端だったコアウィーブ株が6%近く上げて終えたことが、売り方の買い戻しを誘いました。なお、ファンCEOは追加支援の必要性自体は否定しており、市場が警戒する信用リスクとの見方の違いが焦点です。 １６日の株式相場見通し＝自律反発へ、米半導体株下げ渋り買い戻し優勢に +2
■ 米国市場（15日）：ダウ大幅高だがハイテクは重い「ねじれ」
指標終値前日比NYダウ52,177.69+556.21（3日ぶり反発）ナスダック総合26,713.02+20.16（4日ぶり小反発）S&P5007,744.06+25.12（+0.33%）SOX（半導体）11,581.22-103.17／-0.88%・7営業日続落米10年債利回り5.068%-0.121% 10/16の強弱材料 +9
米長期金利の低下や企業決算を手掛かりにヘルスケア・素材株が買われた一方、半導体株指数は7営業日続落。AI関連投資の収益性や資金調達負担への警戒が続き、ハイテク株の戻りは限定的でした。ダウ構成銘柄ではナイキ、ホーム・デポ、ウォルマートが3～4%台の上昇となり、AIや半導体を除く幅広い銘柄に買いが入りました。 media-iryahoo
→ 日本株への含意： 指数は反発でも「AI・半導体だけが売られる」構図が続いており、日経平均の寄与度上位を半導体が占める東京市場には、ダウ高ほどの追い風にはなりません。
■ 米インフレ指標の上振れと「利上げ」観測

ここが従来と大きく違う点です。市場が織り込もうとしているのは利下げではなく追加利上げです。
9月CPI（14日発表）：前月比+0.6%、前年比+3.7%で前年比は市場予想を上回り、コアCPIも前月比+0.3%・前年比+2.6%とともに予想以上。 note

9月PPI（15日発表）：前月比+1.3%、前年同月比+6.3%と前月から伸びが拡大し、前日のCPI同様インフレの根強さを示しました。4年ぶりの高水準です。 yahoozaikei
9月小売売上高：最新週の新規失業保険申請と合わせ、市場は個人消費と労働市場の底堅さを確認しました（※後述の「要注意点」参照）。 yahoo
FOMC：今月27～28日のFOMCでの連続利上げ観測が一部でくすぶる中、16日のウォーシュFRB議長の対談イベントに注目が集まっています。10月FOMCでの2会合連続利上げ観測はくすぶるものの、AI投資を巡る信用不安を背景としたリスク回避の債券買いで米長期金利が低下しています。 yahoozaikei
■ 為替：ドル円は158円台前半でやや円高
15日NY市場の円相場は午後5時現在、前日比32銭円高ドル安の1ドル＝157円94銭～158円04銭。米長期金利の低下を背景に、日米金利差縮小を意識した円買いドル売りが優勢でした。 yahoooanda
NY市場では157円55銭まで下落後158円25銭まで反発し、158円09銭で引け、16日8時時点では158.08円で、本邦勢の本格参入を前に158円台前半でもみ合い。 zaikeimyforex
200日移動平均線が位置する158円台半ば超えでは上値が重く、下値は157円台半ばがサポート。157円台後半～158円台前半でのこう着が続きやすいとみられています。 zaikei

供給不安の中身：EIA週間統計で原油在庫が市場予想を上回って大幅減少したほか、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジアラビアの戦闘、ホルムズ海峡での貨物船沈没が供給不安を高めました。戦略石油備蓄（SPR）を含む原油・石油製品の在庫合計は15億699万9,000バレルと2003年以来の低水準。ホルムズ海峡経由の供給量も引き続き限定的です。 yahoominkabu

米国がイランとの戦闘を再開した場合に大規模爆風爆弾の使用を検討しているとの報道もあり、戦火拡大が懸念されています。 oanda

ロシア要因：ゼレンスキー大統領が15日公開のFTインタビューで、ロシア国内の製油所に対する攻撃を再開すると表明しました。 nikkei

NY金12月限も反発し、前営業日比+81.90ドル（+1.99%）の4,189.80ドルで終了。 diamond

→ 影響： 原油高は空運・陸運・化学株の上値を抑える可能性がある一方、石油関連・商社には追い風です。 media-ir
■ 日銀・G20：本日午後に植田総裁イベントが2つ
これが本日の東京市場最大の国内イベントです。
バンコクで15日に討議を終えたG20財務相・中央銀行総裁会議は、中東情勢の混迷で原油価格が高止まりする中、インフレへの深刻な懸念を共有。各国中銀が物価高退治へ「時機を逃さない利上げ」が重要との認識となりました。 daily
出席した日銀の植田総裁は16日午後、現地で記者会見します。日銀は9月会合で政策金利を1.0%程度から1.25%程度に引き上げており、物価安定に向け利上げを続ける方針も示しています。今月29・30日に次回会合を控え、金融市場は植田氏の発言に注目しています。 oanda
本日15時半には全国信用組合大会での植田総裁あいさつ（内田副総裁代読）も予定されています。 minkabu
前日の下げ要因の一つ：小枝日銀審議委員が15日、「利上げ、過度に慎重にならず」「物価上昇リスクは相応にある」と発言し、2026・2027年度とも物価の上振れリスクが大きくなっているとの認識を示しました。15日の東京市場は米半導体株安に加え、この利上げ観測の再燃がリスク回避を強めた格好です。 経済記事一覧（2026年10月）：時事ドットコム +2

7～9月期の売上高は1兆4,942億台湾ドルで前年同期比50.9%増、純利益は7,630億台湾ドルで同68.7%増。 sbbit

10月16日全球财经晨报：美国通胀与消费数据超预期、加息预期升温，美股反弹但科技股分化，黄金走强，能源供应风险与AI产业兑现能力成为焦点。

核心结论：
市场在消化更高的利率预期，同时重新衡量能源供应风险与AI增长质量；美股和亚洲市场的反弹，仍伴随着明显的行业分化。

【今日主线】
第一条主线：通胀与利率预期。美国PPI、零售销售超预期，美联储官员继续强调通胀风险，今日央行官员讲话及欧美数据将成为美元、债券和黄金的重要观察点。
第二条主线：能源供应与政策缓冲。美国原油大幅去库、柴油供应压力，与国际能源署释放储备并存，油价还需消化能源设施和运输通道风险。A股观察方向包括油气、炼化及航运。
第三条主线：AI产业从扩张转向兑现检验。台积电业绩增长与部分AI企业估值预期下调同时出现，算力需求、融资成本和收入增长需要结合观察。A股观察方向包括算力基础设施、服务器及相关配套。
第四条主线：存储技术与竞争格局。存储股反弹伴随较大波动，4F²技术进展仍需良率、量产和客户认证验证。A股观察方向包括存储芯片、设备及材料。
第五条主线：国内资金收缩与亚洲市场反弹。两市融资余额下降，日韩股市今早高开，中概股及恒指期货夜盘回升，后续关注不同市场之间的情绪传导与A股成交变化。

【美股】
美股周四三大股指收涨，道指上涨1.08%，报52178.99点；标普500指数上涨0.33%，报7744.12点；纳斯达克综合指数上涨0.08%，报26713.03点。标普、纳指均低开高收，道指表现相对突出。
科技股内部走势分化。美光科技盘中一度跌超6%，最终收涨1.8%；CoreWeave一度跌超9%，最终收涨近6%；戴尔跌近7%。
中概股回暖，纳斯达克中国金龙指数上涨1.96%，网易上涨2.7%，京东上涨2.6%。

【宏观】
美国9月PPI、零售销售数据均超预期，通胀与需求韧性继续影响利率预期。克利夫兰联储主席哈玛克警告，若企业和家庭形成高通胀将长期持续的预期，美联储可能需要采取更强硬行动。芝加哥联储主席古尔斯比表示，若通胀来自需求过热或AI数据中心大规模建设，将更令人担忧。
利率市场仍以10月按兵不动为主要预期。CME“美联储观察”显示，10月维持利率不变的概率为71.8%，加息25个基点的概率为28.2%；到12月累计加息25个基点的概率为67.4%，累计加息50个基点的概率为25.4%。
美元指数周四下跌0.49%，收于102.055。纽约汇市尾市，欧元兑美元报1.1212，英镑兑美元报1.3272，美元兑日元报158.14。
美国4周期、8周期国债竞拍得标利率分别为4%和4.05%，均高于前次的3.98%。截至10月9日当周，外国央行持有美国国债减少145.88亿美元。
高借贷成本继续影响美国楼市。30年期固定抵押贷款平均利率维持7.4%，连续八周未下降；美国9月待售房屋签约量环比下降4%。
贸易政策仍有不确定性。欧盟开始评估化工、机械等行业的进口激增情况，可能考虑配额等保障措施。据报道，美墨汽车及金属关税谈判因分歧进展放缓，双方官员表示谈判仍在继续。

【AI存储链】
存储股波动加剧。中信证券研报认为，近期板块受到原油、通胀及利率预期扰动，同时市场开始关注中国本土厂商在服务器DDR5领域的技术进展，以及潜在竞争对海外厂商定价能力的影响。
技术进展仍需与量产能力区分。当前DRAM技术仍以6F²单元结构为主，4F²技术处于早期验证阶段，后续需要观察良率、产量、毛利率及下游客户认证。A股观察方向包括HDD、DRAM、NAND及相关设备材料，重点跟踪技术验证向实际供给转化的节奏。
AI芯片需求继续支撑制造端业绩，台积电第三季度净利润同比增长69%，超出市场预期。台积电证实正与马斯克洽谈Terafab芯片工厂合作，但坚持必须掌握生产运营权。
AI基础设施的融资与现金流受到关注。黄仁勋表示，CoreWeave财务状况持续改善、资本成本正在下降，无需英伟达提供财务担保。与此同时，据路透社援引知情人士报道，Anthropic营收增速放缓，部分投资者讨论的估值约为1.5万亿美元，低于此前约2万亿美元的市场预期。

【科技产业】
AI模型竞争继续推进。Meta发布开放权重模型Muse Spark Open，主要面向编程与AI智能体任务，并与苹果合作支持开发者在Mac设备上本地运行。微软宣布完成MAI-Base-2预训练，其AI负责人称模型规模达到3万亿参数。
工业AI合作扩大。据德国《商报》报道，德国政府计划与英伟达开展大规模合作，拟投入数亿欧元采购算力、训练工业AI模型，西门子、奥迪等约12家企业计划参与。
国内应用端出现新进展。库克表示，苹果智能在华已获批准，将于10月底推出测试版。快手可灵4.0正式全量上线，支持4K、1080p的10-bit HDR输出，单次视频生成最长可达30秒。
谷歌公布Willow量子芯片研究进展，利用“魔态培育”技术将特定量子态错误率降低约40倍，准确度达到99.99%；其在更大规模量子计算系统中的应用仍需进一步验证。
卫星产业方面，欧盟拟加快审查空客、莱昂纳多和泰雷兹共同推进的卫星合资项目。马斯克表示，SpaceX与英伟达联合研发的Star Mind计算机计划于明年量产。

【原油】
国际油价走势分化。WTI原油期货上涨3.03%，收于97.97美元/桶；布伦特原油期货下跌0.13%，收于105.92美元/桶，两油价差显著收窄。国内SC原油主力合约夜盘上涨0.11%，报726元/桶。
美国原油库存大幅下降。截至10月9日当周，EIA商业原油库存减少855.7万桶，远超预期的减少28.8万桶，为2月13日当周以来最大降幅。美国国内原油产量减少30万桶/日至1367.9万桶/日。
成品油供需分化：汽油库存增加351.8万桶，预期为减少80万桶；精炼油库存减少252.7万桶，降幅超过预期。炼厂设备利用率升至93.5%。
能源运输与供应风险仍在。霍尔木兹海峡通行状况存在相互矛盾的官方表述，叠加油轮起火、俄乌能源设施受袭，市场继续关注原油、柴油及航运供应。国际能源署同意释放尚未释放的约1亿桶储备，包括尽快投放2000万桶柴油。印度自10月16日起，对汽油、柴油出口分别征收每升2.5卢比和8.5卢比的暴利税。
美国天然气库存当周增加670亿立方英尺，低于预期的760亿立方英尺，天然气期货盘中上涨3%。

【贵金属】
黄金、白银走强。现货黄金盘中突破4170美元/盎司，日内涨幅达到1.60%；纽约期金盘中上涨2%，报4190.10美元/盎司。现货白银盘中上涨3%，报57.30美元/盎司。

杠杆资金收缩。截至10月15日，两市融资余额合计24661.61亿元，较前一交易日减少313.25亿元。宽基基金成交额两个月来首次突破100亿元，成交活跃度与资金净流向仍需分别观察。

A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY 15 OCTOBER 2026

Here's what actually mattered:

Latest completed US session:
$SPX: 7744.06 (+0.33%)
Nasdaq: 26713.03 (+0.08%)
Dow: 52177.69 (+1.08%)
Russell 2000: 2767.27 (+1.38%)
10Y Treasury: ~5.09%, down about 10bp
Brent: ~$105.92
Gold: ~$4162

The index recovered, but leadership changed. Healthcare and defensive names rose while semiconductor stocks extended their losing streak. The key question is whether this is healthy rotation or the early stages of an AI-capex repricing.

Top 10 Developments

1. PPI delivered a second inflation warning.

September producer prices jumped 1.3% MoM and 6.3% YoY. Energy goods rose 10.8%, but services prices also increased 0.8%. The measure excluding food, energy and trade services climbed 0.5%.

This is the largest monthly headline PPI increase since March 2022. It raises the risk that input-cost pressure spreads into corporate margins and consumer prices. A December Fed hike is now a meaningful market scenario, not a certainty.

2. $TSM reported record profits, but investors wanted more than a beat.

Q3 revenue reached $46.72B, up 41.2% YoY in USD. Net income rose 68.7% in local currency to NT$763.06B. Gross margin was 66.4%.

Q4 revenue guidance: $52.3B-$54.3B.
2026 capex outlook: $60B-$64B.
Advanced nodes of 7nm and below: 79% of wafer revenue, including 8% from 2nm.

$TSM nevertheless fell about 1.8% as management remained prudent about 2027 macro risks. Strong AI demand is real. The valuation and financing debate is separate.

3. AI infrastructure selling continued.

$NVDA fell around 1.8%, $DELL about 6.9% and $HPE about 7.1%. The semiconductor index declined for a seventh straight session.

Investors are separating chip demand from the ability of data-center operators and hardware suppliers to fund expansion profitably. Debt cost, utilisation and free cash flow are now central to the thesis.

4. The market rotated into defensives.

$LLY gained over 3%, $UNH around 2.8% and $WMT about 1.4%. Healthcare led $SPX sectors with a 1.84% gain; materials added 1.71%.

Eight of 11 sectors finished higher. This wasn't a uniform market collapse. It was a meaningful rotation away from crowded AI exposure.

5. September retail sales beat, but the quality was weaker.

Headline sales rose 0.8% versus roughly 0.3% expected. Gasoline-station receipts rose 6.4%; excluding gas stations, sales grew only 0.2%.

A higher dollar value of spending can reflect higher prices rather than greater unit demand. I'm watching real consumption and corporate pricing power, not the headline beat alone.

6. $META and $AAPL made a rare AI collaboration.

$META released Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter open-weight model with 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. It has been optimised to run on two $AAPL M5 Ultra Mac Studios through MLX.

This matters for local AI inference and developer distribution. Model benchmarks and launch availability do not yet prove meaningful new revenue for either company.

7. $RKLB pushed Neutron's inaugural launch into 2027.

Rocket Lab disclosed the delay in an October 14 company update. Shares fell about 6.6% on Thursday.

This is a genuine catalyst reset. Neutron's future launch economics and customer backlog may still be attractive, but delayed testing shifts the revenue timeline and raises execution risk.

8. $PNC showed that bank fundamentals are not uniformly deteriorating.

Q3 net income reached $2.1B, adjusted EPS $5.09 and revenue $6.56B. Net interest income rose 15% YoY to $4.21B. Average loans rose 2% QoQ.

But net loan charge-offs reached $257M and commercial nonperforming loans increased. Strong NII does not eliminate credit-cycle risk.

Chile’s Environmental Assessment Service approves the Punta de Lobos mine’s continuity to 2040, according to Rumbo Minero. Mexico’s Navy reopens Mazatlán to larger vessels.

Global context

Trump says Taiwan agreed to invest up to $4.4 billion in Alaska LNG in the United States and buy 30% of its output for 20 years, according to AFP. However, gCaptain reports that Taiwan has not finalized binding commitments, so the announcement does not establish contracted revenue or secured construction capital. The Washington Post reports that the container ship GFS Pride sank after an attack in the Strait of Hormuz; according to Bloomberg, Brent traded above $106 as attacks threatened Gulf flows.

1. Chile: SEA approves Punta de Lobos operational continuity through 2040

Chile's Environmental Assessment Service (SEA) gave a favorable assessment to the Environmental Impact Study (EIA) for Punta de Lobos' “Operational Continuity through 2040” project, according to Rumbo Minero. The initiative seeks to extend the mine's operations through 2040 at Salar Grande, in Chile's Tarapacá Region.

The project includes US$1.5 million in investment and 124.2 additional hectares of exploitation. Mineria Chilena also reported a favorable assessment for a mining EIA in Tarapacá and described its objective as maintaining the deposit's operational continuity; its publication does not identify the company or detail the investment.

For mining investors, the favorable assessment reduces uncertainty over the deposit's operational continuity. The planned investment and additional area do not establish that production has already increased.

2. Mexico: Navy reopens Mazatlán to larger vessels as Simon weakens

Following the report of Simon as a category 2 hurricane, Mexico's Navy reopened Mazatlán, in Sinaloa, to larger vessels and Puerto Vallarta, in Jalisco, to smaller vessels on October 14. San Blas, in Nayarit, remained closed to all navigation. The notice maintained restrictions on smaller vessels at La Paz, Los Barriles, Loreto, Mazatlán, Teacapán, Nuevo Vallarta and Chacala.

In a subsequent report, the Navy placed Simon in category 1, 262 km southwest of Las Islas Marías and 396 km south-southeast of Cabo San Lucas, with sustained winds of 148 km/h, gusts of 185 km/h and waves of 4–5 meters. The National Hurricane Center (NHC) said Mexico's government had discontinued the hurricane watch for Las Islas Marías and that no coastal watches or warnings remained; it noted that new watches or warnings might be needed for Baja California Sur.

Reopening Mazatlán to larger vessels removes a restriction for shipping lines and shippers, but does not normalize the whole coast: San Blas remains closed and smaller-vessel limits persist. The hurricane's lower intensity does not eliminate the reported waves.

3. Chile: Reuters reports BHP deal with Escondida supervisors to avert strike

Reuters reported on October 14 that BHP and supervisors reached a deal to avert a strike at Escondida, the copper mine operated by the company in Chile. According to La Tercera, the union approved Minera Escondida's proposal, which includes a $30 million bonus per worker alongside other benefits. The outlet describes the operation as the world's largest copper mine.

El Economista (Mexico) reported that 64% of union members approved the company's proposal, averting a stoppage that threatened to disrupt the copper market. In its reports that day, Mineria Chilena said the mine was operating normally and that the regulated collective bargaining process had ended. The reports provide no production figures or details of the agreement's other benefits.

For copper buyers, the reported agreement reduces the interruption risk associated with this negotiation. Reported normal operations do not establish the effect on supply or imply an increase in production: volume figures are missing.

If you want foreign money to stay, don’t sell a tax debate as a tax cut

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stepped up to the mic at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on Tuesday. She said the debate on LTCG and STT is “healthy” and she is “keen” to hear it. She said investors in India and abroad have been commenting on capital gains taxation and that the government is open to hearing their views. She also said she will “tread cautiously” on any commitment because the Budget preparation has already started.

The Sensex jumped 1,100 points. Investor wealth swelled by Rs 1.7 lakh crore. The market heard what it wanted to hear. But here is what actually happened. A microphone opened. A rate did not change. The 12.5% LTCG is still the law. The 20% STCG is still the law. The 12-month holding period is still the law. The finance minister said she will listen. She did not say she will cut. And the market is pricing a cut that has not arrived.

What SBI Research proposed. And why it is not a notification
On Monday, SBI Research released its Ecowrap report. The recommendation was direct. 
“The Government must seriously look into anchoring hot money flows into equity segment by extending the holding period to say 2-3 years and abolishing the long term capital gains tax for equity”. 
The logic is simple. FPI money is hot money. It enters fast. It exits faster. If you extend the holding period required for long-term treatment and remove the tax entirely, investors might stay longer. The volatility might reduce. The rupee might find some support.

But here is what that recommendation is not. It is not a government commitment. It is not a notification. It is not a line in the Finance Bill. 
The Union Budget 2026 maintained the status quo on the 12.5% LTCG rate for listed equities and equity mutual funds. The Finance Ministry has already clarified in Parliament that there is “no such proposal under consideration” to abolish LTCG tax for domestic or retail investors. 
SBI Research is a bank’s research arm. It can recommend. It cannot legislate. The note is a signal. It is not a statute.

Rs 3.04 lakh crore has already left. The Budget has not arrived
Why is this debate happening now? 
Because the outflows are brutal. Foreign portfolio investors have pulled Rs 3.04 lakh crore from Indian equities in 2026 so far. 
That is nearly double the Rs 1.66 lakh crore withdrawn in the entire year 2025. In October alone, FPIs sold Rs 44,166 crore worth of Indian equities. 
Domestic institutional investors pumped in the same amount, absorbing the selling pressure. But domestic buying can support prices. 
It cannot offset the demand for dollars that FPI selling generates. That demand is what pressures the rupee. And the rupee has felt it. The rupee was veering close to its all-time low of 96.96 per dollar last week before the RBI announced emergency measures.

The reasons for the selling are not mysterious. Elevated crude oil prices. A firmer US dollar. Higher US bond yields. And the artificial intelligence rally in North Asian markets, which is pulling capital towards US tech giants and away from emerging markets like India. 
India does not have an AI story that can compete with Nvidia or Microsoft. That is the structural problem. And no tax tweak will fix it.

June already gave foreign bond buyers a tax break. Equities did not get the same treatment
There is an inconsistency here that is hard to ignore. 
In June 2026, the government promulgated an ordinance exempting foreign investors from income tax on interest income and capital gains from government securities under the Fully Accessible Route. 
The exemption was retrospective from April 1, 2025. The result was immediate. FPIs invested Rs 8,795 crore into FAR securities within days. By June 23, foreign investors had poured Rs 35,000 crore into Indian bonds. 
The government proved that tax policy can move capital. It just chose to apply that logic to debt, not equity.

The answer is revenue. LTCG tax on equities is a significant source of government income. Abolishing it would create a hole that would need to be filled. 
And there is no guarantee that the capital that comes in would stay. Hot money can be anchored with longer holding periods. But if the returns are not competitive, it will leave anyway.

She said keeping capital here is not in one minister’s hands. The AI trade is parking it in the US
Sitharaman said the quiet part out loud. 
On retaining foreign capital, she said: “To retain these investments is not a unilateral thing that I can do”. 
She pointed to global capital moving towards frontier AI and US technology companies. 
That is the real story. India is not just competing with other emerging markets. It is competing with the most powerful capital magnet in the world right now. And it is losing.

Global investors have withdrawn around $8.5 billion from India-focused funds in 2026 as capital continues to flow towards artificial intelligence-linked investment opportunities in markets such as South Korea, Taiwan and the United States. India’s weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index has declined meaningfully as investors rotate capital toward Taiwan and Korea. 
The AI trade is not a tax story. It is a returns story. A tax tweak may slow an exit. It will not create an entry. The money that left will not come back because of a 12.5% rate cut. It will come back when the returns are competitive. And that is not something a finance minister can announce.

If you already invest, trade the rule on the books, not the sentence in the headline
The rule that exists is the rule that matters. 
The 12.5% LTCG on gains above Rs 1.25 lakh is the law today. The 20% STCG is the law today. The holding period for equity is 12 months. None of that has changed. The debate is a signal, not a statute. 
Price your portfolio on the tax code that exists. Not the headline that might. The finance minister has opened a conversation. She has not changed a number. Until she does, the only thing that has changed is the noise.

Follow Message for @Wallstreet2Web3

If this breakdown of the capital gains debate and FPI outflows was useful, follow @Wallstreet2Web3 for more data-backed takes on markets, policy, and the money flows shaping India’s economy.

Cheng Lou 开源 Handwired：手写权重，把程序逻辑变成不用训练的神经网络

Midjourney 工程师、前 React 核心团队成员 Cheng Lou 开源了一个自称“玩具项目”的 Handwired：把程序里的 if-else 和循环改写成神经网络的权重。权重是手写的，不用训练，输出和对应的 JavaScript 程序完全一致，在浏览器里就能跑。

原理一行代码就能讲清。比如 result = a > 4 ? 10 : 12，在 a 是整数时可以改写成：

above4 = relu(a - 4) - relu(a - 5)
result = above4 × 10 + (1 - above4) × 12

relu 就是 Math.max(0, x)，神经网络里最常见的激活函数。a 大于 4 时 above4 正好是 1，否则是 0。两个分支都算出来，再用它挑一个。神经网络本质上就是一堆乘法、加法加上 relu，所以程序里的判断和分支，都能收进一个大矩阵乘法里。

也许你会好奇，神经网络的输出不是带概率、不精确吗？

Cheng Lou 的回答是：训练出来的才这样，按程序逻辑手写的权重，同样的输入永远得到同样的输出。

他放了三个 demo。

第一个是 Mini OS，一个有三个窗口和程序坞的小桌面，拖动、缩放、层叠、滚动、文字输入、动画都有。打开浏览器开发者工具看，页面就是普通的网页元素，没有大模型，也没有扩散模型。驱动它的是一个 130 层、9909 个权重的“神经网络”，训练次数为零，在浏览器里用 CPU 实时计算。

第二个是实时搜索 10 万份 JSON 文档，每敲一个键重搜一遍。正则匹配、JSON 解析、高亮全是这种手写网络，再转成 WebGPU 代码放到显卡上并行跑。项目文档里的实测（Apple M5 Max + Chrome）：每次搜索 11 到 15 毫秒；浏览器自带的正则引擎一般 8 到 28 毫秒，遇到容易回溯的写法要 2 秒多。文档写明两者谁快说不准，所以页面把两个时间都列出来。浏览器不支持 WebGPU 时会退回 CPU，搜一遍要 13 秒。

第三个是会“学习”的相册。整个程序可微分，也就是能用训练神经网络的反向传播来调参数。你在左边画几个矩形当草图，右边的照片布局由一个小网络算出，它的 244 个参数随着你拖动实时训练。损失函数里加了一项对齐惩罚，照片会自己往一条线上靠，没有任何代码专门去对齐它们。参数很少，训练全在 JavaScript 里跑。

Cheng Lou 还设想，把一段 Handwired 程序接到 nanoGPT（Andrej Karpathy 的一个小型 GPT 训练项目）这样的模型上一起训练，模型既能写莎士比亚，又能精确执行那段程序。这个目前只是 README 里的设想，仓库里没有现成实现。

代码以 MIT 许可开源，demo 直接在网页上打开就能玩。想自己写，需要装 Bun，克隆仓库后从 template 目录的开关按钮示例开始，文档里有完整教程。

推文说“把普通 JS 代码变成神经网络”，容易让人以为能把现成代码丢进去自动转换。项目文档写的是：没有工具能把已有的 JavaScript 源码转成网络。你要用它提供的构建函数，把逻辑一句句写成比较、选择、加权求和这类操作。网络每次都要把所有操作跑一遍，不能提前退出，也不能跑运行时才知道次数的循环，所以常见的循环得改写成计数、树形合并之类的结构，文档专门用一章讲怎么改。所有数都是 32 位浮点数，每个值的取值范围要事先声明。

项目主页：https://t.co/ywg9dzrFbM
GitHub：https://t.co/fg1sj0trv4
原推文：https://t.co/QW2cMnSiWE

SubQ Snap does well in what TypeSafe calls the "Danger Zone", context above 32k. 85% of tokens processed by Snap are from requests above 32k, with many shipping data-intensive features to prod. SSA keeps long context fast and cheap.

We are open-sourcing Decision LCR (Snap 74%, Jev 58%), which mimics real-world tasks and is adapted from AA-LCR.

Because long-context benchmarks for decision models don't really exist, we built one of our own by adapting Artificial Analysis' Long-Context Reasoning benchmark, which we think does a better job mimicking real-world tasks than many LLM long-context benchmarks, to a decision format. We are open-sourcing this today.

Decision LCR: https://t.co/JGGSEBBczF

Adapted from Artificial Analysis's AA-LCR. 100 human-written questions over real 72K–115K-token document sets, converted into 118 decisions, each run with three option orderings to control for position bias. Chance is 19.2, and models score 24–25 with the documents removed.

We'd love for others to run it, use it and improve it. If you work on long-context evaluation or decision models, we'd value your feedback and collaboration.

To learn more about SNAP and our evaluation process, check out the blog:  https://t.co/CglHueOxnv

Meta 发布开放权重模型 Muse Spark Open：免费下载能商用，本地跑要两台 512GB 内存的 Mac Studio

Meta 10 月 15 日发布 Muse Spark Open，模型权重可以直接下载，按 Muse Model License 免费使用，商用也行。Meta 称它是“迄今最强的美国开放权重模型”。

Muse 系列推出以来，主力模型 Muse Spark 和三天前发布的 Muse Wonder 都只能通过 Meta 的产品和 API 用，开放权重的只有小模型 Muse Glimmer。这是 Meta 第一次放出大尺寸 Muse 模型的权重。

模型总共 8160 亿参数，处理每个 Token 只动用其中 420 亿，这种结构叫混合专家（MoE），算得快，但整个模型还是要全部装进内存。上下文 100 万 Token，能读文字、图片、视频和音频，输出文字，主打写代码和让 AI 长时间自己干活。

【能不能下载，能不能商用】

能下载。Hugging Face、亚马逊 SageMaker、Google Cloud Model Garden 和微软 Foundry 都提供权重。Hugging Face 上要先登录填申请表，写真实姓名、出生日期和完整机构名称，提交后不能改。

能商用。许可证允许使用、修改、微调、蒸馏（用它的输出训练别的模型）、再分发和出售，不收费。条件有三条。

第一，用了它的产品要在界面、文档、网站或设置菜单里显著标出“Built with Muse Spark Open”。

第二，遵守附带的使用政策：不能用于军事、武器、关键基础设施等高风险用途，不能在没有执业资格时提供金融、法律、医疗专业服务，也不面向 18 岁以下用户。

第三，卖模型接口的大公司要单独签协议。具体是：你把它或基于它改的模型通过 API 之类的方式卖给别人调用，而你的公司连同关联公司过去 12 个月总营收超过 2000 万美元，就要先通知 Meta、另签协议。算的是公司总营收，不只是这项业务的收入。

把它嵌进自己的 App 做功能、公司内部用、做研究，都不受第三条限制，公司多大都一样。Llama 当年的许可证门槛是月活 7 亿用户，这次换成了针对模型接口生意的营收门槛。

【普通电脑能不能跑】

跑不了。模型卡写的要求是：压缩到英伟达 4 位精度格式 NVFP4 的版本至少要 700GB 显存，原始 BF16 版本要 2TB。

Meta 说它针对两台 M5 Ultra Mac Studio 做了优化：每台最多 512GB 统一内存，两台连起来凑出 1TB，用苹果的 MLX 框架运行。官方没写在 Mac 上跑的是哪个压缩版本，也没给速度。

有服务器的开发者，SGLang、vLLM、TensorRT-LLM、llama.cpp 等主流推理框架都能跑，也可以用 PyTorch 和 TorchTitan 微调。

没有这种硬件，就调 API：Baseten、Fireworks AI、Groq、Modal、Nebius、OpenRouter、Together AI 提供接口，价格由各平台定，Meta 没公布。

【和其他模型比怎么样】

Meta 只拿它和开放权重模型比：美国的 Inkling（前 OpenAI CTO Mira Murati 创办的 Thinking Machines 出品）和英伟达 Nemotron 3 Ultra，法国的 Mistral Large 4，中国的通义千问 Qwen3.8、智谱 GLM 5.3、月之暗面 Kimi K3。以下成绩都来自 Meta 的模型卡。

第三方机构 Artificial Analysis 的综合智能指数，Muse Spark Open 39 分，Inkling 26，Nemotron 3 Ultra 23，“美国最强”说的是这一层。放到全部开放权重模型里，它低于 GLM 5.3 的 45 和 Kimi K3 的 44，和 Qwen3.8 的 40 接近。Artificial Analysis 开源榜目前排第一的是小米 MiMo-V2.6-Pro，46 分，Meta 的对比表里没有它。

单项领先的是调用工具和难题推理：测模型通过 MCP 协议调外部工具完成任务的 MCP-Atlas，89.2 分，对手最高 84.5；不借助工具做“人类最后的考试”（HLE，一套极难的跨学科考题），26.1 分，对手最高 22.2。

写代码偏弱：命令行任务 Terminal-Bench 76.4 分，Kimi K3 85.0、GLM 5.3 83.9；软件工程任务 DeepSWE 60 分，Kimi K3 68、GLM 5.3 67。

最突出的是防越狱。StrongREJECT 测的是模型被人诱导时会不会输出有害内容，分数越低越安全，它是 0.5 分，其他模型都在 60 分以上。Meta 说开放权重版额外做了安全训练。

和自家闭源模型比，Meta 三天前引用的 Artificial Analysis 数据里，Muse Wonder 52 分，Muse Wonder Full 56 分，Muse Spark Open 低一截。

原文：https://t.co/SICKXtdZyV
官方博客：https://t.co/bMJ4GKl0An
模型卡：https://t.co/oqcXeL9Ol0

この確率は、寄り付き前の指数・先物・金利・原油の動きから推定した主観的な数値です。

寄り天と寄り底を合わせると70％となるため、方向感のない展開よりも、寄り付き後に一方向へ動く展開をやや重く見ています。

### TOPIX優位か、日経平均優位か

日経平均優位

# 65％

TOPIX優位

# 35％

今朝の先物は日経225miniが＋1.71％、TOPIX先物が＋1.19％です。

前日の急落では日経平均の下落率が大きかったため、日経平均への寄与度が大きい銘柄群に買い戻しが入れば、日経平均が相対的に強くなる可能性があります。

ただし、寄り付き後にNT倍率が再び低下するなら、TOPIX優位へ判断を修正する必要があります。

### 資金ローテーションの見立て

現時点では、次のように整理します。

- 半導体： 米国のSOXが続落しており、資金流入を確認できない。
- 銀行： 米国・日本の長期金利低下が影響するため、金利だけでは買い優勢と判断できない。
- 商社： 原油高は資源関連に支援材料となる可能性があるが、市場全体のリスク回避が重荷。
- 海運： 中東情勢の緊迫化は運賃上昇要因になり得る一方、燃料費や航路変更などのコストにも注意が必要。
- グロース株： 先物の反発率が低く、リスク選好の回復はまだ限定的。

現段階では、半導体から銀行・商社・海運へ明確に資金が移ったとは確認できません。

本日の寄り付き後は、業種別の騰落率と売買代金を見て、単なる先物の買い戻しか、実際に資金の流れが変化しているかを判別する必要があります。

## 5．10月16日の日経平均レンジ予想

予想レンジ：64,800～66,500円

メインシナリオ：65,300～66,000円

前日の現物終値64,425.95円に対し、今朝の日経225先物miniは65,530円です。

先物に沿って寄り付くなら、前日の急落から反発して始まる展開が想定されます。

ただし、WTI原油が97.55ドルへ上昇し、SOXも－0.88％となっているため、上昇が一日を通して続くと決めつけることはできません。

また、日経VIが36.13まで上昇していることから、想定レンジ内でも上下に大きく振れる可能性があります。

## 6．シナリオ別確率

以下は、寄り付き前に確認できる市場材料に基づく主観的な推定です。

| シナリオ   | 確率  | 想定レンジ          | 主な根拠                     |
| ------ | --- | -------------- | ------------------------ |
| メイン    | 40％ | 65,300～66,000円 | 急落後の買い戻しと戻り売りが交錯         |
| 上昇     | 25％ | 66,000～66,500円 | 米金利低下、先物の買い戻しが継続         |
| さらなる上昇 | 10％ | 66,500～67,000円 | 半導体の下げ止まり、原油高の一服、買い戻しの拡大 |
| 下落     | 18％ | 64,800～65,300円 | 半導体売りの継続、寄り付き後の戻り売り      |
| さらなる下落 | 7％  | 64,000～64,800円 | 原油の一段高、金利再上昇、先物売りの再加速    |

確率の合計は100％です。

### 上昇シナリオの根拠

日経225miniが65,500円近辺を維持し、65,800～66,000円を回復できることが条件です。

米10年債利回りが5.0％前後で安定し、TOPIX先物も4,047を上回って推移するなら、反発が続く可能性があります。

### さらなる上昇シナリオの根拠

66,500円を上回るには、先物の買い戻しだけでなく、現物市場にも買いが広がることが重要です。

SOXの下落が止まり、NASDAQ100がプラス圏へ転じ、原油価格も落ち着くことが望ましい条件です。

さらにTOPIXやグロース株にも買いが広がれば、反発の持続性が高まる可能性があります。

ただし、現時点では半導体が弱く、WTI原油も上昇しているため、確率は10％にとどめます。

### 下落シナリオの根拠

寄り付き後に65,300円を維持できず、日経225miniが下落へ転じる場合です。

半導体関連の売りが継続し、TOPIX先物も4,000を下回る方向へ動くなら、前日の下落が一時的なものではなく、売り圧力が続いている可能性があります。

### さらなる下落シナリオの根拠

WTI原油が100ドルに近づく、または米10年債利回りが再び上昇するうえ、SOXの下落が続く場合です。

原油高によるインフレ懸念、金利上昇、半導体売りが同時に進めば、株式市場への下押し圧力が強まる可能性があります。

日経平均が64,800円を明確に割り込み、先物も安値を更新する場合は、64,000円近辺まで下値警戒を広げます。

## 7．1時間ごとの値動き予想

寄り付きは65,500円前後を中心に想定します。

前日の急落後であるため、始値そのものよりも、寄り付き後に65,300円を維持できるか、66,000円を回復できるかを重視します。

| 時間帯         | 日経平均の想定レンジ     | 注目点            |
| ----------- | -------------- | -------------- |
| 8:00～8:45   | 65,200～65,800円 | 先物と寄り前気配の変化    |
| 8:45～9:00   | 65,300～65,900円 | 寄り付き注文の偏り      |
| 9:00～10:00  | 64,900～66,000円 | 買い戻しと戻り売りの強さ   |
| 10:00～11:00 | 65,000～66,100円 | TOPIXも反発できるか   |
| 11:00～12:00 | 65,000～66,100円 | 前場の安値・高値を更新するか |
| 12:00～13:00 | 65,100～66,100円 | 後場寄りの需給        |
| 13:00～14:00 | 65,100～66,300円 | 買い戻しが継続するか     |
| 14:00～15:00 | 64,900～66,400円 | 原油・米株先物・為替の動き  |
| 15:00～15:30 | 64,800～66,500円 | 引けに向けたポジション調整  |

この時間別レンジは、寄り付き前の価格と想定シナリオから作成した推定であり、実際の値動きを保証するものではありません。

特に重要なのは9時～10時です。

65,300円を維持しながら66,000円を試すなら反発継続を重視しますが、65,300円を割り込み、TOPIX先物も下げに転じる場合は下落シナリオを優先します。

## 8．地政学リスク：織り込み済み・未織り込み

### 織り込み済みと考えられる要素

- 中東情勢の緊張による原油価格の上昇。
- WTI原油が97ドル台にあることによるインフレ懸念。
- 海上輸送ルートのリスクに対する市場の警戒。
- 原油高が企業コストや金融政策に影響する可能性。

Reutersは10月15日、WTIが在庫減少などを背景に上昇し、ブレント原油も100ドルを超える水準で推移したと報じています。

[image](https://t.co/RXhHiJ6fbc\&sz=32)

https://t.co/UtzPsDQ5St

+1

### 未織り込み、または追加的な下落要因になり得る要素

- WTIが100ドルを超え、その水準が定着すること。
- ホルムズ海峡などの主要輸送ルートで供給障害が長期化すること。
- 中東の軍事行動が拡大し、原油供給が実際に大きく減少すること。
- 原油高によるインフレ再加速で、米国債利回りが再び上昇すること。
- 半導体株の下落が長期化し、AI関連投資への懸念が市場全体に波及すること。

これらのリスクは、発生を前提とするものではありません。

既に市場が認識している地政学リスクと、実際の供給途絶などによって新たに価格へ反映されるリスクは分けて考える必要があります。

## 9．寄り付き後に確認するポイント

1. 日経225mini：65,500円を維持できるか。 反発が続くか、再び売りが強まるかを判断する基準です。
2. TOPIX先物：4,047近辺を維持できるか。 日経平均だけでなく、広い銘柄群にも買いが広がるかを確認します。
3. NT倍率：16.11倍から反発するか。 上昇なら日経平均優位、低下ならTOPIX優位を示す可能性があります。
4. SOX：11,581.22から下げ止まるか。 半導体の下落継続は日経平均の反発を抑える要因です。
5. 米10年債利回り：5.0％前後で安定するか。 再上昇すれば、成長株・半導体への逆風が強まる可能性があります。
6. WTI原油：97.55ドルからさらに上昇するか。 100ドルに近づく場合は、インフレ・金利経由のリスクを強めに評価します。
7. グロース250先物：759円から上昇が広がるか。 グロース株にも買いが広がれば、市場全体のリスク選好回復を確認しやすくなります。
8. 日経VI：36.13から低下するか。 低下すれば急落後の不安が和らぐ可能性がありますが、高止まりなら値幅拡大への警戒を続けます。

## 最終判定

10月16日は、前日の大幅下落を受けて日経平均が反発して始まる可能性が高いと考えます。

米国債利回りの低下、米国株の反発、日経225miniの上昇が支援材料です。

一方、SOXの続落、WTI原油の上昇、日経VIの急上昇から、全面高への転換を確認するにはまだ材料が不足しています。

- 日経平均予想レンジ：64,800～66,500円
- メインシナリオ：65,300～66,000円
- メインシナリオ確率：40％
- 寄り天確率：35％
- 日経平均優位の確率：65％
- 相場の主な動き：急落後の買い戻し。ただし半導体は警戒継続
- 最大の下落リスク：原油高、半導体売りの継続、金利再上昇

本日は、日経平均が上昇するかだけでなく、TOPIXやグロース株にも買いが広がるかを確認することが重要です。

records.text:
Meta が10月15日、総パラメータ816B（8,160億）のAIモデル「Muse Spark Open」の重みを公開しました。

Muse Spark Open は816B中42Bだけ動き、KVは1トークン約250KBです。
KV（過去の入力を覚えておくメモリ）が小さいので、長い文書も扱いやすい設計です。

Muse Spark Open は画像も扱えるネイティブマルチモーダルのモデルで、文脈長は最大1Mトークンです。
Meta は Apple と組み、M5 Ultra 搭載の Mac Studio 2台（1台あたり統合メモリ最大512GB）で動かせるようにしました。

自社内でAIを動かす選択肢を検討している方に、直接関係する話です。

まず、計算とメモリの食い違いです。
Muse Spark Open は MoE（専門家を切り替える構造）です。
各層に256個のエキスパートがあり、1トークンごとに8個だけを選びます。
エキスパートは全パラメータの約97%を占めます。

そのため1トークンあたりの計算は42B級で済みます。
一方で、どの8個が選ばれるかは入力ごとに変わるので、256個すべてをメモリに載せておく必要があります。
BF16（16ビットの数値形式）の重みは約1.5TBです。
Hugging Face の検証では、3ビットに量子化（数値を粗く圧縮）した版が、M3 Ultra（512GB）の Mac 1台に約344GBで載りました。
機材の見積もりは、動く42Bではなく全体の816Bから始めてください。

次に、1Mトークンでもメモリが収まる理由です。
注意機構は GQA（KVを複数の問いで共有する方式）です。
問いを担うクエリは128ヘッドですが、KVは16ヘッドしかありません。

KVの量は 2×16ヘッド×64次元×62層＝126,976値／トークンです。
BF16で約250KB、1Mトークンで約266GBです。
KVをクエリと同じ128ヘッドで持てば8倍の約2.1TBになり、512GBの Mac 2台の合計を超えます。
長い契約書や規格文書を丸ごと読ませたい方ほど、16ヘッドの設計の恩恵を受けます。

最後に、手元で動かす条件です。
・BF16：H200 8枚×4ノード（テンソル並列32）
・NVFP4（4ビット形式）：B200 1ノード
・Mac：M5 Ultra の Mac Studio 2台＋MLX

「Mac で動く」は512GB構成2台の話で、一般的な Mac の話ではありません。
ライセンスは Muse Model License で、商用条件に制限があります。完全なオープンソースとは別物です。
推論の思考は止められず、low/medium/high/xhigh が内部で16/64/256/512に対応します。

クラウドのAPIで足りている方は、今日することはありません。
社内で動かす方は、機材より先にライセンスの商用条件を確認してください。

MoE の機材は、動くパラメータではなく全パラメータで決まります。

① mksglu/context-mode  ★29,753
コーディングエージェントのコンテキスト窓を最適化するツールです。ツール出力をサンドボックスに隔離して98%削減し、セッションの記憶を永続化、MCPとフック経由で17プラットフォームのルーティングを強制すると説明されています。TypeScript製・独自ライセンス、forkは2,079、2026年2月23日の作成から昨日まで更新が続いていて、公開先は https://t.co/xA62ZChT0y、未処理のissueは359件。トピックには mcp、claude-code-hooks、codex、opencode、zed-extension といった語が並びます。
圧縮そのものより、減らしたあとに「どこへ何を流すか」を強制する側を売りにしているのが面白いところだと分析します。長いログを捨てる話はもう珍しくありませんが、捨てた後の経路まで決めてしまうのは、運用で効いてくる順番かなと思います。うちの夜間ジョブのログ量を見ていると、ちょっと他人事ではありません。

ブラウザを抱える重さはエージェント運用でいちばん効くコストなので、そこに手を入れる道具が増えているのは自然な流れかなと思います。同じAPIで乗り換えられるなら試す価値はありそうですが、互換性の実態は自分で確かめないと分からないところだと見ています。

10月15日、米連邦取引委員会（FTC）がOpenAIとAnthropicに対して、AIの安全インシデントをめぐる50ページ規模の民事調査要求を送ったと報じられました。同じ日の別報道では、アイオワなど米8州がChatGPTが若年ユーザーに害を与えたとしてOpenAIを提訴し、制裁金などを求めていると伝えられています。訴状では不正アクセスやサイバー攻撃に関わる事案にも触れ、同社が安全性を後回しにしていると指摘されているとのことです。
